revisions: A marker cannot be created at LocalConversation._tree_stamping: UserPromptSubmit hooks can replace a MessageEvent after that convenience stamp, constructing a fresh event without preserving id/timestamp/parent. The durable marker seam must be inside ConversationState.append_event after its authoritative _stamp_parent_id and before EventLog.append.

One-event R7 is unsound. HookEventProcessor can synchronously emit HookExecutionEvent values through original_callback before the outer action/message reaches the default callback. These nested events can all be durably appended inside one outer ConversationState save context before one deferred base_state flush. R7 must journal an ordered consecutive pending-event chain.

Each journal entry can bind expected EventLog index, final stamped event id/parent, exact event JSON digest, and a deterministic candidate base-state payload/digest for that durable prefix. Startup may recover the exact present prefix; it must never infer a markerless orphan or use unique-descendant structure as intent authority.

Fernet encryption makes independently reserialized base snapshots byte-unstable. Therefore _save_base_state must serialize once, upgrade the journal immediately before the base write with that exact payload/digest, write those exact bytes, and clean the marker only after successful write. This makes base-save-before-cleanup detectable by exact digest.

Agent-server recovery has to run immediately after ConversationLease.claim and before _scrub_persisted_credentials or LocalConversation construction. Current startup otherwise can rewrite stale base_state before repair. ConversationLease.guarded_write can fence the local marker/base writes by generation.

Recovery accepts a well-formed marker from any strictly older lease generation, not only G-1, because repeated takeovers may crash before mutating recovery state. Same-generation same-owner re-entry remains intentionally unresolved/fail-closed in the model.

observations: Stock TaskManager is a concrete Arc<Mutex<HashMap<...>>> implementation. TaskContext privately contains that same TaskManagerInner Arc<Mutex>, and spawn always creates a fresh UUIDv4. No TaskStore/create-or-get backend trait was found in the exact released source search.

ServerHandler call_tool/get_task/update_task/cancel_task are overrideable application-level methods, so a persistent task implementation is possible only by implementing/replacing task behavior at the handler/application layer rather than by swapping storage under stock TaskManager/TaskContext.

ToolRouter.call is the reusable policy/validation surface: it rejects disabled routes and runs registered extractors/argument deserialization. A custom task-capable call_tool should route normal validation/policy through ToolRouter rather than reimplementing it manually.

The generic Service dispatcher checks Tasks client capability only after call_tool returns a Task response, so that guard still cannot serve as a pre-materialization fence for a custom persistent task row.

ToolCallContext carries RequestContext, arguments, inputResponses and requestState, so a custom handler can inspect continuation identity before task materialization while still constructing the router context. This does not provide stock restart durability or idempotent create-or-get by itself.
rmcp_persistent_backend_seam.boundary: The smallest released seam is application-level ServerHandler + ToolRouter composition with a custom persistent task store/executor. Stock TaskManager cannot simply be pointed at durable storage while retaining TaskContext semantics. Such a resident server/store remains a strict Phase-1 unresolved executor/storage dependency.
